newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CELEBRATE ANOTHER ASHES TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CELEBRATE ANOTHER ASHES TRIUMPH.

text.p: Australia underlined their domination of England's cricketers by winning the fifth test by 264 runs on Sunday and so securing their fifth successive series victory.
The latest Ashes thrashing, coming in the penultimate over of the fourth day at Trent Bridge, was the result of another sorry English batting display as the hosts were bowled out for 186.
After Australia had taken their overnight total of 167 for four to 336 all out -- courtesy of more poor bowling -- they systematically carved their way through the fragile English ranks.
Only Graham Thorpe, who was left unbeaten on 82, showed any sort of application as England faced the prospect of batting for a day and-a-half to save the match.
Wickets fell at regular intervals and it only needed the extra half-hour, claimed by skipper Mark Taylor, to finish the job.
Victory was completed when Devon Malcolm edged Glenn McGrath to Mark Waugh in the slips to spark noisy celebrations in the Australian ranks.
Australia's bowlers shared the wickets with three each for McGrath, Shane Warne and Jason Gillespie and one for Paul Reiffel.
The morning session had seen more misery for England as Ian Healy (63), Warne (20) and Reiffel (22) piled on the runs at will, making England's afternoon performance look all the more inept.
The result leaft the tourists with an unbeatable 3-1 lead in the six-match series with the last test at The Oval beginning on August 21.
Australia have held the Ashes since 1989 and, apart from a brief blip when they were defeated in the first test at Edgbaston, never looked like losing them in this series.
England were saved by the weather next time out at Lord's after being bowled out for 77 but then lost heavily at Old Trafford (by 268 runs) and Headingley (innings and 61 runs).
"Australia played the better cricket and deserved to win the game and the series," said England captain Michael Atherton, who failed again on Sunday, managing just eight before being caught behind.
"As they've proved over the last 18 months they are the best team in the world."
Atherton's position must be under threat but he refused to be drawn after the match, saying only: "We'll wait and see. I've always said I'll know when it's time to go."
His opposite number Taylor also faced calls for his head early in the summer but has silenced the critics with another superb leadership display.
"To say I'm delighted is an understatement," he said. "It's a fantastic feeling, especially for the captain. We were one-down in the series, but I said at the time there was no need for panic.

"As a unit, it's probably the best side I've played in. We've got some fine batsmen, two or three good strike bowlers, the world's best leg-spinner, plus an outstanding wicket-keeper in Ian Healy, who was a good choice as man of the match here."
Taylor hinted that he would be tempted to stay on if wanted. "I'd want the support of the Board and the selectors that I'm still the best man for the job," he said.
Atherton meanwhile must decide whether he wants to take on a daunting trip to the West Indies early next year.
